To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NSAIDs may be useful to prevent the onset of Alzheimer's disease (AD) in APOE4 carriers.
NSAIDs are effective in the prevention of AD only if given at very early stages of AD pathogenesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel NSAIDs with anti-inflammatory properties and with the ability to reduce Aβ production and aggregation.
understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying the beneficial effects of NSAIDs in AD, and with the design and conduct of clinical trials with NSAIDs for the treatment and prevention of AD.

the following issues: 1) the biological mechanism of NSAID action in the early stages of AD; 2) the optimal NSAID regimen for AD prevention; 3) the safety and efficacy of NSAID treatment in cognitively impaired subjects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NSAIDs should not be prescribed to patients with established AD or mild cognitive impairment.
NSAIDs should be used to treat AD or mild cognitive impairment.
NSAIDs may have a beneficial effect only in the very initial stages of AD, but their chronic use may be harmful in patients already affected by AD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NSAIDs may have a role as primary prevention in AD, but not as secondary prevention in AD and mild cognitive impairment.
NSAIDs are not useful in the treatment of mild-to-moderated AD or mild cognitive impairment.
the use of NSAIDs in the early stages of AD could be effective, but not in the later stages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chronic use (at least for 2 years) of naproxene may be useful to protect cognitively normal subjects with a family-history of AD from the development of AD.
the long-term use of NSAIDs in the very early stage of AD could be beneficial.

the use of NSAIDs for the prevention and treatment of AD is a promising approach, but it is necessary to identify the most appropriate NSAID, the most appropriate dose and the most appropriate time of administration.
